book.title: Appeasing Hitler: Chamberlain, Churchill and the Road to War
book.summary: The Sunday Times Bestseller 'Astonishing' ANTONY BEEVOR 'One of the most promising young historians to enter our field for years' MAX HASTINGS On a wet afternoon in September 1938, Neville Chamberlain stepped off an aeroplane and announced that his visit to Hitler had averted the greatest crisis in recent memory. It was, he later assured the crowd in Downing Street, 'peace for our time'. Less than a year later, Germany invaded Poland and the Second World War began. This is a vital new history of the disastrous years of indecision, failed diplomacy and parliamentary infighting that enabled Nazi domination of Europe. Drawing on previously unseen sources, it sweeps from the advent of Hitler in 1933 to the beaches of Dunkirk, and presents an unforgettable portrait of the ministers, aristocrats and amateur diplomats whose actions and inaction had devastating consequences.

argument.statement: Indecision, failed diplomacy, and parliamentary infighting enabled Nazi domination of Europe and contributed to the outbreak of the Second World War.

book.rationale: The book provides a historical account centered on the politics and decisions leading to World War II, making History the primary focus, while also addressing the political dynamics and military implications involved.
